interpretation: Post-label method development on the existing 100 claims. Counter-map outputs and their gold-joined performance did not exist when this configuration was frozen.
question: After removing every originally retrieved document and exact duplicate without using origin, does a fresh retrieval view provide a safer signal for choosing same-model RAG versus closed-book?

scope.activation: All 363 cached same-model endpoint disagreements from evidence_signal_v1.

retrieval.query_plan: Reuse the victim's ten cached claim-only Stage 1 queries; no endpoint, evidence, or condition is used to generate them.
retrieval.exclusion: Remove all document IDs present in the original top-k and all documents with exact text matching an original result. Do not inspect origin when excluding.
retrieval.candidate_semantics: For each query, select the nearest five eligible documents, then remove documents already returned for an earlier query without backfilling. This matches Stage 1 fresh-document semantics.

superseded_offline_pilot.issue: The first implementation backfilled five fresh documents after cross-query deduplication, yielding exactly 50 documents per row and exceeding the Stage 1 selection semantics.
superseded_offline_pilot.disposition: Retained as an unscored offline artifact. No LLM call was issued. V2 fixes the candidate budget before any counter-map output.

private_pre_output_diagnostic.purpose: Verify origin-blind exclusion and quantify whether a genuinely less-exposed view was created; poison annotations remain forbidden from prompts and decisions.

evaluation.primary: Endpoint-selection accuracy on exclusive disagreements, grouped by claim, compared with the answerability cascade and original passage-map signal.
evaluation.secondary: Whole-system clean and per-rate accuracy when agreements pass through unchanged.
evaluation.next_gate: Run a final same-model arbiter only if the counter view adds selection signal or clean protection beyond endpoint calibration alone.
